name: Mozambique
summary_text: Mozambique demands real caution from trans visitors — one of Africa's better legal positions. Same-sex conduct was decriminalised under the 2015 Penal Code; courts ruled in 2017 that LGBTIQ organisations can register (Lambda Mozambique); and there is no documented pattern of police targeting. Counterweights: no legal gender recognition, no SOGI hate-crime statute, social hostility outside Maputo is significant, and the Cabo Delgado insurgency affects the north (a general, not trans-specific, risk). For a visitor: no legal exposure; modest infrastructure; avoid the north.

sources.title: Mozambique | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity decriminalised under the new criminal code effective June 2015; courts ruled LGBTIQ organisations can register (2017); employment discrimination based on sexual orientation illegal since 2007 (Law 23/2007) but trans and intersex people not explicitly protected; no legal gender recognition procedure, making trans people particularly vulnerable; societal attitudes broadly neutral but family ostracisation and employment/education challenges occur; during 2024 campaigning the opposition PODEMOS leader pledged to address 'the issue of sexual and ethnic minorities'.

UNDP report (Dec 2024) 'African Commission Resolution 275: Ten Years of Advancing LGBT+ Rights in Africa' - regional framework document assessing country obligations, protective environments, access to justice and civic space across African states.

sources.title: Gay Mozambique News & Reports
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz archive of Mozambique news and reports (2006-2011): the first newspaper article arguing for gay rights (2006), the first national gay-rights seminar, LAMBDA's registration struggles, constitutional-amendment efforts, and refugee risks.

sources.title: Africa's most and least homophobic countries
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (March 2016): Afrobarometer survey of Africa's most and least homophobic countries - Mozambique among the most tolerant (56% would welcome a homosexual neighbour), behind Cape Verde (74%) and South Africa (69%).

sources.title: After 10 Years of Legal Battles, Mozambique’s Only LGBT Organization Takes a Step Closer to Legal Recognition · Global Voices
sources.claim_summary: Global Voices (Nov 2017): after 10 years of legal battles, the Constitutional Council ruled Lambda's status did not violate the constitution - since 2008 the Justice Ministry had ignored Lambda's registration applications; a step toward legal recognition for Mozambique's only LGBT organisation.

sources.title: Mozambique LGBT activists move on to next battle after anti-gay law scrapped | Mozambique | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (June 2015): Mozambique's new penal code scrapped the colonial-era 'vices against nature' provision; Lambda's Carina Capitine: 'The LGBT community is not targeted by violent acts as in some African countries. But we do face discrimination here.'
